meta: You type one sentence: "Sum up yesterday's meeting notes in Drive, then schedule a follow-up on Friday." That sentence goes through two MCP sockets. What's inside? An MCP connection has a client and a server.

muc.title: One sentence, two sockets
muc.text: You type: sum up yesterday's meeting notes in Drive, then schedule a follow-up meeting on Friday. That sentence goes through two MCP sockets. Let's open them up.

muc.title: Client and server
muc.text: An MCP connection has two sides. One side is the MCP client, inside the AI app you're chatting in. The other side is each tool's MCP server: one for Drive, one for the calendar.

muc.title: Tools, resources, prompts
muc.text: Each server offers three kinds of things. Tools to do things, like creating an appointment. Resources to read, like files. And prompts, ready-made prompt templates.

muc.title: What have you got?
muc.text: When they first connect, the client asks: what have you got? The server sends back a list of tools, with a description of each. AI reads that list, like the tool board on the wall in part one.

muc.title: One step at a time
muc.text: Then AI goes step by step: it sends a tool call to the Drive server to read the notes, sums them up, then sends a tool call to the calendar server to create the meeting. Creating an event changes your data, so the app asks you first.

muc.title: One task, two tools
muc.text: Turn on a ready-made connector like Drive or a calendar. Give AI a task that needs both at once, and watch it call each one in turn.

muc.title: What if you install anything?
muc.text: Every server opens a door into your data. What if you install just anything? Part four: using MCP safely.
